episode_title: A Conversation with Tekedra Mawakana, Co-CEO of Waymo

real_qa.q: What safety improvement has Waymo achieved compared to human drivers in crash reduction?
real_qa.r: When Waymo was at 127 million fully autonomous miles, they established a 10x reduction in injury-causing or worse crashes than human driving in those same areas. Around pedestrians, they are 12 times safer than humans. A study with Swiss Free, an insurance company, found that the Waymo driver was 12 times safer than a human in most instances.
real_qa.requete: Waymo safety record crash reduction compared to human drivers

real_qa.q: How many autonomous rides and trips per week is Waymo currently operating at scale?
real_qa.r: Waymo is operating over 400,000 trips per week. This represents significant growth from 200,000 trips per week just last year. Over the lifetime, Waymo has given 20 million rides, with 15 million of those given in 2025 alone.

guest.bio_context: Tekedra joined Waymo in 2017 as Global Head of Policy and became Co-CEO in 2021. She oversees commercialization, scaling the business, and navigating complex regulatory and market environments. Before Waymo, she held senior leadership roles at Yahoo and eBay, and began her career as an intellectual property lawyer advising on telecommunications and regulatory matters.

real_quote: We're not doing fast and breaking things, but earning trust and winning for the long term.
key_stats: 20 million total rides given over lifetime
10x reduction in injury-causing or worse crashes versus human drivers at 127 million autonomous miles
12x safer around pedestrians than human drivers
$16 billion raised in Series D funding
40,000 road deaths in United States per year
1.2 million road deaths globally per year
Waymo planning to launch in Tokyo and London in 2026
